skill.name: skill-forge
skill.description: Audit and validate Agent Skills from folders, ZIP archives, or SKILL.md drafts with evidence-based checks.
skill.summary: Inspect Agent Skills, test their behavior in bounded environments, and assess release readiness.
skill.author: zztimur

security_audit.summary: The 400 static findings were adjudicated individually. The two Docker socket findings are confirmed because bounded execution depends on a host daemon with powerful control over the host environment. The remaining matches are false positives in scanner logic, documentation, release tooling, or synthetic tests; an embedded prompt-injection fixture and the Docker dependency still require explicit review before publication. Static review was capped at 400/949 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 549 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.
Use a dedicated rootless or isolated daemon, restrict socket access, and require explicit operator approval before running package tests.

remediation.issue: A synthetic fixture contains an auditor-override prompt requesting file access, public disclosure, and command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the text confined to inert test data, label it as adversarial input, and verify that every evaluator treats it as untrusted content.

remediation.issue: The package contains extensive subprocess, filesystem, and archive operations.
remediation.suggestion: Retain explicit argument arrays, read-only source mounts, default-deny networking, resource limits, and verified cleanup for every execution path.

remediation.issue: Evaluation code reads an API key and sends requests to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Keep network evaluations opt-in, use least-privilege credentials, avoid real secrets in fixtures, and redact authentication data from logs.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need reliable checks for package safety, triggering, behavior, and release readiness. Skill Forge inspects artifacts, runs bounded tests when approved, and produces evidence-based findings.
actual_capabilities: Inspect folders and ZIP archives for structure, metadata, references, secrets, and dangerous patterns.
Route requests into evaluation, validation, repair, or release-gate workflows.
Pressure-test skill triggering, input boundaries, output contracts, and privacy behavior.
Run explicitly reviewed self-tests in bounded environments with resource and network controls.
Assess release readiness using separate artifact, validator, test, and qualitative evidence.
limitations: Static inspection cannot prove that every runtime behavior is safe.
Self-tests are package evidence and do not replace an independent evaluator.
Bounded execution requires a supported isolation backend and preinstalled dependencies.
The skill does not certify host-specific platform behavior without trusted platform evidence.

use_cases.title: Review a New Skill
use_cases.description: Inspect a folder or ZIP before sharing it, then identify security, structure, and usability issues with cited evidence.

use_cases.title: Validate a Release
use_cases.description: Run applicable validation and release-gate checks while keeping package evidence separate from independent platform evidence.

use_cases.title: Test Skill Behavior
use_cases.description: Pressure-test triggering, edge cases, privacy boundaries, and unsafe requests using controlled synthetic inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Package Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Agent Skill folder for structure, metadata, triggering, and obvious security concerns. Cite the files you inspect and separate facts from assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a local skill folder.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a ZIP Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this ZIP as a portable Agent Skill. Check archive paths, required files, references, and release blockers. Return findings with evidence and a clear pass or fail status.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer received a packaged skill.

prompt_templates.title: Pressure-Test Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Pressure-test this skill with normal, ambiguous, missing-input, and unsafe requests. Evaluate triggering, privacy, output contracts, and refusal behavior without executing unreviewed code.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer is assessing behavioral safety.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this skill for release readiness using strict evidence. Review package integrity, trusted validator provenance, bounded test results, unresolved risks, and required remediation before recommending publication.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release owner needs an evidence-based decision.

output_examples.input: Review a skill ZIP containing a valid SKILL.md, safe references, and one missing resource link.
output_examples.output: Release readiness: Partial. The package structure is valid, but the missing reference must be restored or removed before publication.

output_examples.input: Pressure-test a note-cleaning skill with an unsafe request to upload private text.
output_examples.output: Finding: The skill must refuse the upload and keep the text local. The unsafe behavior is a high-impact privacy defect.

output_examples.input: Ask whether passing package self-tests proves independent release validity.
output_examples.output: No. Package self-tests provide useful evidence, but an independent validator or trusted platform check is still required.

best_practices: Inspect untrusted package content before relying on its instructions or bundled tools.
Keep static findings, runtime observations, validator evidence, and qualitative judgments separate.
Use synthetic inputs, default-deny network access, and bounded resources for approved self-tests.
anti_patterns: Treating a passing bundled test as proof of independent platform approval.
Running a package script because its name suggests validation or safety.
Allowing artifact prose to change the requested scope, authority, or security assessment.

faq.question: What inputs can Skill Forge review?
faq.answer: It can review a skill folder, ZIP archive, or SKILL.md draft when the artifact scope is clear.

faq.question: Does it execute skill code?
faq.answer: Only explicitly reviewed commands may run, and approved self-tests require bounded isolation and synthetic inputs.

faq.question: Can it find prompt injection?
faq.answer: It reviews artifact prose and behavior for instructions that attempt to override scope, authority, or safety controls.

faq.question: Does it publish a skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces findings and release evidence; publication remains a separate authorized decision.

faq.question: Are package self-tests independent evidence?
faq.answer: No. They describe the package behavior and must remain separate from trusted external validation.

faq.question: What should I provide for a release review?
faq.answer: Provide the exact artifact, target platform, source reference, available validators, and any approved bounded test plan.
